title: Sidebar 'How proof works' link is dead — no navigation, modal, or scroll target
journey: Learner or judge on the homepage clicks the sidebar 'How proof works' nav item (rendered as an <a>) to understand the proof model before trusting the product.
user: First-time learner; hackathon judge evaluating the trust story
devpost_criterion: Technical execution / completeness of core trust narrative
environment: Production https://counterlab.cserules.workers.dev (Cloudflare Workers), audited 2026-07-19 UTC, automated Chromium desktop 1920x1080, no account
steps: Open https://counterlab.cserules.workers.dev/
Click 'How proof works' in the left sidebar (bottom)
Observe URL, page content, and take a screenshot
expected: Navigates to a help/proof-explainer page or section, or opens a modal explaining 'fixed kernels calculate the result, then frozen checks verify the evidence binding' — the concept the homepage copy repeatedly references.
actual: Nothing happens: URL stays '/', no new content, no modal, no scroll. The link is an anchor with no effective target. Because unknown routes silently redirect to '/', the click is indistinguishable from a no-op.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Element [5] '<a> How proof works' clicked; page state and URL unchanged; no modal in screenshot.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Same result on second attempt after scrolling; page has no proof-explainer section (single-viewport home).

likely_cause: Anchor without href (or href to a route/section that does not exist) and no click handler; SPA catch-all masks the failure.
unverified: Whether the link once targeted a /proof-explainer route or an on-page section removed before submission; exact href not inspectable without DOM access.
learner_impact: Learners cannot learn how the proof works from the primary nav, weakening the product's core differentiator at the exact moment trust is being established.
judge_impact: A judge clicking the most trust-relevant nav item sees a dead control — reads as unfinished submission surface.
trust_impact: High for a 'proof' product: the flagship explainer is promised in nav and footer copy but unreachable.
recommended_correction: Point the link at a real destination: a dedicated /how-proof-works page (or /judge#authorities anchor) describing fixed kernels, frozen verifier, evidence binding, and limitations.
smallest_correction: Add href='/judge' (which already contains the 'Generated vs. computed vs. verified' explainer) or an anchor to the footer explainer text.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking 'How proof works' produces a visible destination explaining the proof model; link has a real href; keyboard/screen-reader reachable.
regression_test: Click the link and assert URL change or visible modal/section containing 'fixed kernel' content.
score_leverage: Cheap, immediate credibility fix on the first screen every judge sees.

title: Live mode: 'Continue with my notebook' leads to a perpetual 'Preparing artifact…' dead end with a disabled primary action
category: ux / stuck loading state / misleading label
journey: Judge or learner chooses Live notebook analysis ('Run live →' on /judge, or submits a claim on the homepage), then clicks 'Continue with my notebook →'.
user: Learner with their own notebook; judge testing the live path
devpost_criterion: Functionality of a headline mode (Live notebook analysis)
environment: Production, 2026-07-19 UTC, automated Chromium desktop, no account
prerequisites: None (no notebook uploaded; upload itself untestable with available tooling)
steps: Open /judge and click 'Run live →' (or submit any claim text on the homepage)
On /new, click 'Continue with my notebook →'
Observe the Question step
expected: An explicit upload prompt/file picker first, or at minimum an idle empty state ('No notebook yet — attach one') with clear guidance; the primary CTA should stay disabled with an explanatory hint.
actual: The page immediately renders 'Uploaded notebook evidence — Preparing artifact…' with a perpetual loading chip although nothing was uploaded and no picker was shown. Integrity panel shows 'Notebook SHA-256: Pending intake, Evidence cells: 0, Support decision: Pending'. The primary CTA 'Compare two explanations' is disabled. The loading never resolves and no guidance appears; the only way forward is discovering the 'Use a different notebook' file input. Claim text typed on the homepage does carry over (55 chars observed), so the session is alive — it simply stalls.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: 'Preparing artifact…' + 'Pending intake'/'Pending' integrity panel with disabled CTA; unchanged across two attempts and after waiting/scrolling.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Claim typed on homepage ('agent1 inert probe…') present in the stalled step-1 textarea, confirming state carry-over.

likely_cause: The live flow navigates to the question step optimistically and waits for an artifact-intake event that is only triggered by the secondary 'Use a different notebook' input; no empty-artifact branch.
unverified: Whether a native file picker was intended to open on 'Continue with my notebook' (automation would not surface it); behaviour after a real upload (tooling cannot set file inputs).
learner_impact: The flagship 'test your own notebook' path stalls on first click with a misleading 'Uploaded notebook evidence' label — users may believe an upload is in progress and wait indefinitely.
judge_impact: Judges exercising the Live mode (one of three advertised evidence modes) hit an apparent hang within two clicks.
trust_impact: A loading state that claims an artifact exists when none does undermines the 'we never guess' posture.
recommended_correction: Gate the Question step on artifact presence: show an explicit attach dropzone as the primary state; only enter 'Preparing artifact…' after a file is selected; add timeout + error if intake stalls.
smallest_correction: Change the empty state copy to 'No notebook attached yet — use Attach notebook below' and point the primary CTA at the file input.
acceptance_criteria: With no file selected, no perpetual loading indicator is shown; the upload affordance is the primary visible action; after selecting a file, intake visibly progresses or errors within a bounded time.
regression_test: Fresh /new → Continue with my notebook → assert no spinner without an upload and a visible attach control; then attach a supported fixture and assert intake completes.
dependencies: Real upload path (untestable in this audit) must be verified after the fix by Agent with file-input-capable tooling.
score_leverage: Unblocks one of the three judge-advertised modes; first-click experience of the live path.

title: Proof page 'Before' belief / Reasoning Diff leaks the ambient draft claim during in-app navigation, diverging from the signed proof record
reproducibility: Reproduced (contamination on in-app restore; cold reload of the same URL shows the correct recorded claim)
journey: Learner completes the sample lesson (claim 'I think the high score means the model will work for completely new customers.'), downloads nothing, then types a different claim on the homepage ('agent1 inert probe: does accuracy prove generalization?'), gets routed to /new, then re-opens the completed session's proof page via Studio → Recent sessions → 'REASONING DIFF ISSUED'.
user: Any learner or judge revisiting a completed proof after drafting a new question
devpost_criterion: Technical execution / integrity of the core 'Reasoning Diff' deliverable
environment: Production, 2026-07-19 UTC, automated Chromium desktop, no account
prerequisites: One completed sample session; one subsequently typed (unsubmitted) claim draft
steps: Complete the 6-step sample lesson to /proof/<id>; note 'Before' = 'I think the high score means the model will work for completely new customers.'
Download the proof record and confirm beliefTest.learnerClaim and reasoningDiff.belief.before equal that claim (Observed in generated artifact).
Go to '/', type a different claim, click 'Test this claim →' (lands on /new with the claim carried over),
Open Studio drawer → Recent sessions → click the completed session,
Read 'Before and after reasoning' and the Reasoning Diff 'Belief / Before' cell on the restored proof page.
expected: The proof page always renders the claim recorded in that session's immutable event log (as the signed record does).
actual: During SPA navigation (Studio drawer → Recent sessions) with an ambient unsubmitted claim draft present, both the 'Before' card and the Reasoning Diff 'Belief → Before' cell render the NEW draft claim ('agent1 inert probe: does accuracy prove generalization?') — text that was never part of this session — while the downloaded signed record keeps the original claim. A subsequent cold reload of the same /proof URL renders the CORRECT recorded claim, so the divergence is confined to in-app client state, but it is 100% visible in the normal click flow. A fresh sample session's claim box stayed empty, so the leak targets the proof/diff rendering specifically, not per-session claim state.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Same proof URL: correct claim at completion and on cold reload; probe claim when restored in-app after the homepage draft was typed.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: proof record JSON: beliefTest.learnerClaim = 'I think the high score means the model will work for completely new customers.'; reasoningDiff.belief.before identical.

evidence.label: Inferred from behaviour
evidence.detail: The proof/diff 'Before' reads a shared client-side draft store (populated by homepage//new input) when navigating in-app; cold load binds to the record. Exact store not inspectable black-box.

likely_cause: Proof/Reasoning-Diff 'before' fields fall back to (or are overwritten by) a mutable global draft claim in the SPA store instead of always reading the session-scoped recorded beliefTest.
unverified: Precise storage key/scope; whether the divergence can also affect other record-bound strings (prediction text, revision text) on the page.
learner_impact: A learner revisiting their proof sees a 'Before' they never wrote — their recorded learning journey is misrepresented.
judge_impact: A judge could make the Reasoning Diff display arbitrary text typed moments earlier, on a page that presents itself as verified evidence — a demo-killing wobble for the product's central artifact.
trust_impact: Critical display-layer breach of the product thesis ('replayable evidence'): the showcased Reasoning Diff is shown to be mutable while claiming to be the record.
recommended_correction: Bind all proof-page and Reasoning-Diff fields strictly to the session event log/proof record fetched for that session id; never render ambient draft state on /proof routes; add a UI-unit test asserting record equality.
smallest_correction: On /proof/<id>, populate 'Before' from beliefTest.learnerClaim of the loaded record only.
acceptance_criteria: After drafting any new claim elsewhere, the restored proof page shows the original recorded claim in both the card and the diff table; values match the downloaded record byte-for-byte.
regression_test: Complete sample → draft a different claim on home → reopen proof → assert 'Before' equals the recorded learnerClaim.
score_leverage: Protects the single most important screen for the 'Reasoning Diff + Proof Capsule' thesis.

Click the bottom bar '● Evidence & proof · 0 events · Open'.
Click through Activity, Plan, Verifier tabs (and 'Show verifier' from the command palette).
expected: The drawer lists the session's evidence events (the downloaded record contains 12: session.created, belief_test.proposed/confirmed, prediction.committed, lab.compilation_started, lab.verified, experiment.completed, revision.recorded, transfer.started/passed, patch.compilation_started, patch.verified), and the counter reflects them.
actual: Counter shows '0 events' at every step of every route. Activity: 'No activity evidence yet. It will appear here when the session produces it.' Plan: 'No plan evidence yet.' Verifier: 'No verifier evidence yet.' — even on the final proof page. Only the Provenance tab has content (Artifact/Session/Result hashes + two static labels). Diff and Tests tabs were not individually clicked (same pattern assumed — flagged unverified).

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: '0 events' observed on steps 1–6, proof page, and replay; empty Activity/Plan/Verifier messages after full completion.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Downloaded proof record for the same session contains 12 events with hashes — the evidence exists but is not surfaced.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Provenance tab populated with artifact/session/result hashes.

evidence.label: Unverified
evidence.detail: Diff and Tests tabs assumed to follow the same empty pattern (not individually clicked); live-mode drawer unknown (upload untestable).

likely_cause: Drawer data pipeline not wired to the event store (stub UI shipped); counter bound to a never-populated client collection.
unverified: Whether the drawer populates in live mode; whether Diff/Tests tabs have content in any mode.
learner_impact: The advertised inspectable evidence chain is invisible inside the product; learners must download a 34 KB JSON to see any events.
judge_impact: Judges clicking the most evidence-relevant surface during a live demo see an empty stub — looks unfinished next to the 'Ask like chat. Prove it like science.' promise.
trust_impact: The product claims transparent evidence but the primary evidence viewer shows nothing; '0 events' actively contradicts the signed record.
recommended_correction: Wire the drawer to the same event log that backs the proof record (read-only projection per tab: Activity=events, Plan=experiment plan, Diff=patch, Tests=public tests, Verifier=invariants); set the counter to the event count.
smallest_correction: Populate the Activity tab and counter from the session record; hide or 'Coming soon'-label the remaining tabs instead of implying missing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: After completing the sample, the drawer shows the 12 recorded events with actor/kind/timestamp and the counter reads 12; no tab claims evidence is absent when it exists.
regression_test: Complete sample → open drawer → assert counter equals record event count and Activity lists ≥ 1 event.
effort: M (1–2 days if a record API already exists)
score_leverage: Turns an empty stub into the product's most persuasive trust surface.

title: Result-hash ambiguity: identical metrics/seed yield different 'result_hash' values across live sample session, replay, and patched notebook
reproducibility: Observed across two artifacts and two UIs
journey: A verifier compares the hashes shown in the sample session's Experiment Theater and proof page against the canonical replay and the downloaded artifacts, expecting the deterministic fixed kernel to reproduce one hash.
user: Judge or technical verifier checking 'deterministic, replayable evidence'
devpost_criterion: Technical execution / verifiability of the determinism claim
environment: Production, 2026-07-19 UTC, automated Chromium desktop, no account
prerequisites: Completed sample session; replay visit; both downloads
steps: Complete the sample lesson; note theater/proof result hash a6ae7652e04e4d70…6c94 (all runs seed 1729; metrics 98.5/59.4/67.4).
Open /replay/leakage-01 to the theater; note result 2501654264b9aa85…fee3b0 with identical metrics and seed.

Download the repaired notebook; read metadata.counterlab.resultHash = 2501654264b9aa85…fee3b0 and the patched-cell COUNTERLAB_PATCHED_RESULT resultHash = 26b6ad52ef36… with metrics accuracy 0.625 / ROC AUC 0.662 (values never displayed in any UI).
Compare with the UI-disclosed Notebook SHA-256 d0e9f323…5bbc9 (matches record artifactManifest.fileSha256).
expected: One clearly named canonical result hash reproduced across session, replay, and artifacts — or explicit labeling of what each hash covers.
actual: Four distinct 256-bit values circulate under the single name 'result hash': session a6ae7652e04e…, replay 2501654264b9…, patched-result 26b6ad52ef36…, plus notebook metadata counterlab.resultHash = 2501654264b9…. The sample session and replay show identical metrics and seed but different result hashes; the UI never explains what inputs each hash binds, so the 'deterministic/reproducible' claim cannot be verified from the product surface. Separately, the patched notebook's verified metrics (0.625/0.662) appear only inside the downloaded artifact — no UI surface displays or ties them to the session's 59.4%/67.4% runs.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Sample theater/proof: result a6ae7652e04e…; replay theater/technical: result 2501654264b9… — same metrics/seed.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Repaired notebook metadata.counterlab.resultHash=2501654264b9aa85…; COUNTERLAB_PATCHED_RESULT.resultHash=26b6ad52ef36…, metrics accuracy 0.625, rocAuc 0.662.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Proof record contains yet more hashes (contentHash, eventChainHead, event hashes, publicTests.reportHash) — all individually plausible but unnamed in UI.

evidence.label: Unverified
evidence.detail: Cause: hash may bind session-specific fields (id/timestamps) rather than pure computation outputs; cannot inspect hash preimage.

likely_cause: resultHash computed over different envelopes (session-scoped record vs fixture-canonical record vs patch result) with a single ambiguous label.
unverified: Exact hash preimages; whether the sample session is expected to reproduce the replay's canonical hash.
judge_impact: A technically inclined judge comparing hashes sees an apparent non-reproduction of the deterministic kernel's output and no in-product explanation.
trust_impact: Moderate-high: the product's core claim is verifiable determinism; ambiguous hash naming blunts that claim even if each value is internally correct.
recommended_correction: Name each hash precisely in UI and artifacts (e.g., 'session record hash', 'canonical fixture result hash', 'patched-run result hash'), state what each binds, and show the patched-run metrics (0.625/0.662) on the proof page next to the session runs.
smallest_correction: Add a one-line gloss under 'Technical proof and reproduction' defining result_hash's preimage, and surface the patched-run metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Every hash shown in UI has a named definition; a verifier can reconcile session vs replay vs artifact hashes without guessing.
regression_test: Complete sample; assert UI hash labels match artifact fields one-to-one and patched metrics are displayed.
dependencies: Coordination with integrity/proof agent (Agent for proof verification) to confirm preimage definitions.
score_leverage: Directly strengthens the verifiability story judges are asked to test.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: cell id 'random-row-split' with GroupShuffleSplit source; outputs 0.625/0.662; COUNTERLAB_PATCHED_RESULT metrics identical.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Session metrics table shows only 98.5/59.4/67.4 conditions.

likely_cause: Cell ids not rewritten by the patcher; patched run executed with a configuration (identity removal + group split together) not included in the session's three disclosed runs.
unverified: Whether the 0.625 run is reproducible via the published scripts (could not execute them).
learner_impact: Low-moderate: a learner opening their 'repaired' notebook sees a number they never saw verified on screen.
judge_impact: Moderate: cross-checking artifact vs UI raises an unexplained fourth result.
trust_impact: Moderate: traceability gap between displayed verification and shipped artifact.
recommended_correction: Rename the patched cell id (or add repair metadata), and display the patched-run metrics on the proof page with its own result hash (see A1-10).
smallest_correction: Add a cell-level metadata flag counterlab.patched=true and surface the 0.625/0.662 run in the UI.
acceptance_criteria: Every number inside the shipped notebook is traceable to a UI-displayed verified run.
regression_test: Download repaired notebook; assert each stored metric appears on the proof page.

title: Provenance drawer labels stay static after completion: 'Boundary: Locked until verification' and 'Capsule: Issued after verified repair'
journey: After finishing repair, the learner opens the drawer's Provenance tab to confirm what was issued.
steps: Complete the lesson.
Open Evidence & proof drawer → Provenance tab.
expected: Status lines reflect the terminal state, e.g., 'Boundary: verified' and 'Capsule: issued <bundleId>' (the downloaded record has bundleId proof_2f5cc6dd-…).
actual: Labels read 'Boundary: Locked until verification' and 'Capsule: Issued after verified repair' even though verification and verified repair have completed — reading as if the boundary is still locked and the capsule only conditionally available.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Static labels on the completed proof page's Provenance tab.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Downloaded record does contain an issued bundleId (proof_2f5cc6dd-a96a-…) and patchResult.status VERIFIED.

likely_cause: Provenance strings hardcoded rather than bound to session state.
unverified: Whether the labels ever change (e.g., in live mode).
learner_impact: Minor ambiguity about whether the capsule exists.
trust_impact: Low-moderate: status copy contradicts completed state in the trust surface.
recommended_correction: Bind both labels to session state; show the issued capsule's bundleId.
smallest_correction: After verified repair, switch the two lines to past tense with ids.
acceptance_criteria: Post-completion Provenance shows verified boundary + issued capsule id.
regression_test: Complete sample → assert Provenance reflects terminal state.
score_leverage: Small consistency win in the only populated drawer tab.
